title.narrative: The Australian Volunteers Program-global development cooperation-July 2017-June 2027

description.narrative: The Australian Volunteers Program deploys Australians who volunteer their skills through assignments with overseas partners across 26 countries in the Pacific, Asia and Africa across diverse sectors including health, education, disability and gender inclusion, climate, economic growth and recovery. The goal of the program is that global volunteering supports locally led change and the realisation of the Sustainable Development Goals. The program is delivered by Australian Volunteers International (AVI) in consortium with DT Global and Alinea International.

title.narrative: Formative evaluation of the Australian Volunteers Program’s thematic ‘impact areas
Independent Evaluation of the Australian Volunteers Program

description.narrative: Cambodia's Eye Care Foundation (ECF) works to eliminate avoidable blindness and vision impairment, in conjunction with the Cambodian Ministry of Health, local health departments, and hospitals. In 2022-23, under the Australian Volunteers Program, Marguerite Goulding worked as a Program Development Mentor volunteer with ECF to support its strategic planning, to provide technical support and develop training resources. Her work helped build ECF’s brand and reputation and enabled the organisation to receive key funding. Some of that funding has supported renovations to the eye health unit in Mondulkiri Provincial Hospital, and to enable improvements to the hospital’s eye care services, including eye screening, eye surgery, and cataract surgical rates. According to ECF, Marguerite and her extensive knowledge of eye health has been a tremendous asset to the organisation. ‍ Please note ALL data provided in this submission relates to reporting period 1 July 2022- 30 June 2023.

Fiji: ‍ The Commonwealth Local Government Pacific (CLGF) was established to improve the way local government operates in the Pacific, focused on advocacy, leadership, structures, systems, policies, institutional strengthening and gender mainstreaming. The Australian Volunteers Program has supported CLGF through multiple volunteer assignments focused on implementing the Pacific Partnership – New Urban Agenda. The pillars of the Agenda include sustainable urbanisation and job creation, livelihoods and improved quality of life. These volunteers have also provided technical support on sustainable urbanisation issues, complementing the limited pool of urban development specialists in the Pacific.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Indonesia: ‍ The Australian Volunteers Program has supported the Institute of Resource Governance and Social Change in Kupang through several assignments and a small grant. The most recent volunteer assignment in 2022 supported business development and financial supply chains for Small Medium Enterprises, covering the seaweed supply chain and focused on women. The volunteer’s support has positively impacted the women farmers and the broader farming community in Savu Island, by reducing seaweed cultivation cycles and improving seaweed survivability rates. The replication of this project in other coastal villages and the interest generated among seaweed farmers demonstrates the potential for widespread adoption.

Tanzania: ‍ ECHO East Africa is a training centre helping organisations and community development workers in efforts to reduce hunger. ECHO was provided with a A$9,731 impact grant from the Australian Volunteers Program to improve food security and nutrition to nomadic pastoralist communities of northern Tanzania. The project started in January 2023 and provides training and necessary resources (seeds) for women in these communities to establish perennial vegetable gardens.

The Australian Volunteers Program demonstrated significant impact through supporting the Kiribati School and Centre for Children with Special Needs (KSCCSN), the nation's only educational institution serving children with disabilities. ‍ Two Australian volunteers provided crucial mentorship to strengthen the organisation's capacity to support around 330 students. An English Language Teacher Mentor, focused on strengthening teaching strategies through workshops and individual support, improving language learning outcomes for both teachers and students. ‍ The second volunteer, serving as Finance and Administration Mentor, enhanced KSCCSN's financial management practices through grant application assistance, budget preparation, and establishing financial policies. His work strengthened financial stability and increased donor confidence. ‍ Both volunteers joined KSCCSN's management team, participating in board meetings and liaising with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade. Their collaborative efforts enhanced the school's educational effectiveness whilst advancing disability inclusion and accessibility in Kiribati's education system.

The Australian Volunteers Program enhanced health systems capacity in the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) through targeted support for inclusive healthcare delivery. ‍ The program supported a speech pathologist to undertake a one-year assignment with the FSM Department of Health and Social Services, developing an Early Development Checklist for screening children aged two months to four years. This milestone screening tool enables early diagnosis of disability and autism spectrum disorder (ASD), facilitating timely interventions. The volunteer customised the forms to be culturally and linguistically appropriate for remote staff use. ‍ The Early Development checklist was successfully implemented in Pohnpei State, earning recognition from health authorities and improving developmental milestone monitoring. She also conducted ASD workshops for parents and health and education staff, providing communication strategies and enhancing understanding of ASD. ‍ These initiatives strengthened the department's capacity to deliver inclusive programs addressing marginalised groups' needs, improving early childhood development services and aligning with broader objectives of promoting equity, accessibility, and social inclusion within FSM's health system.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: The Australian Volunteers Program strengthened organisational capacity for Live & Learn Cambodia (LLC), which supports vulnerable communities including women, youth, people with disabilities, and indigenous groups in building climate resilience and disaster preparedness. ‍ During LLC's significant growth period (2022-2024) following COVID-19 restrictions, three Australian volunteers provided strategic support. ‍ A Monitoring and Evaluation Mentor, enhanced LLC's ability to meet contractual obligations by supporting the development of monitoring frameworks, program plans, and training activities. ‍ On a remote volunteer assignment, a Management Information System Mentor reviewed operational management processes, identifying technology solutions and cost-effective cloud-based platforms. ‍ The third volunteer provided Internal Policy Development mentoring, updating critical policies including Human Resources, Financial Management, Procurement, Staff Safeguarding, GEDSI, and Child Protection. ‍ This comprehensive volunteer support enabled LLC to continue expanding its climate change mitigation and adaptation work, helping more Cambodians overcome poverty and reduce climate vulnerability.

The Mongolian Association of Sign Language Interpreters (MASLI) advocates to improve the legal environment for the deaf community, trains interpreters and undertakes interpretation services. MASLI sought support from the Australian Volunteers Program to develop a training program for interpreters and provide guidance to the Mongolian government and local NGOs to improve sign language legislation. Australian volunteers Ramas McRae and Rebecca Ladd worked with local educators, conducted research, and assisted the deaf community and local NGOs to deliver information sessions and advocacy activities, and connected MASLI with organisations in Australia and overseas. As a result of their assignments, MASLI has deepened its knowledge, and expanded its sign language interpreter training programs, including pioneering a train-the-trainer program for deaf individuals aspiring to become interpreter trainers. According to MASLI, Ramas’ and Rebecca’s contributions have showcased the immense capabilities of deaf individuals to the broader mainstream community and advanced sign language interpretation in Mongolia.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: The farming community in Bantul, Indonesia has been heavily impacted by climate change. Local NGO Pemberdayaan Perempuan Memerangi Kemiskinan (PPMK) has been supporting 200 women in Bantul through microfinancing to run small businesses to support themselves and their families. PPMK selected 30 of these women to participate in a project funded by a small grant from the Australian Volunteers Program. Through workshops and in-home visits the women learnt about organic farming, planting trees, soil health, waste management and the impacts of climate change. The grant supported the women to set up organic vegetable gardens and composting using plastic products from around their homes. Many of the women reported being unaware of climate change and the consequences of burning waste and disposing garbage in rivers prior to the project. Through sharing their experiences with family, friends and partners, PPMK estimates around 120 people in total were reached by the project.

Timor Leste: ‍ AMT (Asosiasaun Maluk Timor) works to improve the health care system of Timor-Leste, through support to local doctors, nurses and health care workers. The Australian Volunteers Program has continued its long-term support of AMT with three assignments in 2022-23, focused on women’s health and social care, tuberculosis, and nurse mentoring. The nurse mentor volunteer helped strengthen primary health care services in Timor Leste by providing triage training and equipment to community health centres in three municipalities (Dili, Ermera and Oecusse), as well as developing a framework and curriculum to upskill primary health care staff.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Tonga: ‘Ahopanilolo Technical Institute (ATI) is a vocational education and training Facility. In 2022 ATI launched a Tourism & Hospitality Labour Mobility Pathway in collaboration with the Pacific Labour Facility, Australian Pacific Technical College, and the Tongan Ministry of Internal Affairs. The program aims to supply tourism and hospitality workers to meet labour mobility demands including under the Australian Pacific Labour Scheme. An Australian Volunteer assisted in developing this training program and provided on-going mentoring for ATI staff to ensure the program’s sustainability. The first group of graduates were available for work placements in Australia from June 2023.

Vanuatu: ‍ The Australian Volunteers Program provided support to the Vanuatu Ministry of Health in infectious disease prevention and control through three volunteer assignments. With support from these volunteers, the Ministry developed Infection Prevention Control Boards for the Vila Central Hospital. The Boards provided up to date information to staff, helped improve hand hygiene, and contributed to an improved audit rating for the hospital. These volunteers also supported the Ministry to implement a health information system which will provide accurate data on vaccination progress across Vanuatu and help implement the Vanuatu National Action Plan for Viral Hepatitis.
